title: postfix ! is accepted in a concise arrow body whose arrow declares a Result channel
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Accepted Placements': 'A `!` on a Result operand MUST be accepted if and only if all five hold', condition 1 being that every enclosing node out to the nearest statement or arrow function is one of exactly seven forms. The walk in condition 1 stops at 'the nearest statement OR ARROW FUNCTION'. An arrow function is therefore a STOP, not a rejection: the propagation returns from the arrow, which is the function whose declared channel condition 3 is asking about, and here that arrow spells `Result<string, Missing>`. 07-must-consume/a-concise-arrow-body-returning-a-result-is-a-return pins the must-consume half of the same reading — `=> e` is a `return`. This case pins the placement half, and it is deliberately the spelled-contract spelling so that condition 3 is satisfied by an authored annotation rather than by inference.

xfail.reason: the fork reports SMITHERS1204@11:58 and refuses the program. Its `safeUnwrapPlacement` answers `false` whenever the placement walk stops at an arrow function, on the stated ground that 'a concise arrow body has no statement list to hoist a guard into'. That is an implementation limit, not the rule: condition 1 names the arrow function as one of the two places the walk STOPS, and the reference lowers the form by giving the arrow a block body. Closing it needs the fork to synthesise that block body — a real lowering feature rather than an entry in a table of shapes. MEASURED, not inferred: `<scratchpad>/conv/probes/stmt07-concise-arrow-with-contract/main.sm` on both backends, js runs and prints `Ada Lovelace`, go reports SMITHERS1204. This case PINS CURRENT BEHAVIOUR on the reference; it is not a regression on either side.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx, 'Accepted Placements', condition 1: the walk runs 'until the nearest statement or arrow function', so an arrow body terminates the walk rather than failing it.
